newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY UNION-INJURED FITZPATRICK GIVEN LATE DEADLINE.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-INJURED FITZPATRICK GIVEN LATE DEADLINE.

text.p: New Zealand captain Sean Fitzpatrick has until just minutes before the start of Saturday's test against Australia to prove his fitness, All Blacks coach John Hart said on Thursday.
The New Zealand hooker is struggling to recover from a knee injury aggravated during last Saturday's epic 35-32 win over South Africa in the opening match of the Tri-Nation series.
Fitzpatrick hobbled into Melbourne with the rest of the squad on Tuesday and later pleaded with team management to give him more time to recover.
"My knee's getting better every day. I'm just really grateful that John's given me until match day," he said.
An orthopaedic surgeon who examined Fitzpatrick on Tuesday was quoted in Australian newspapers as describing the joint as "being through the tyre and now down to the hub cap".

Hart was initially sceptical about the chances of his captain recovering in time for the second match of the Bledisloe Cup series, which New Zealand can clinch after their 30-13 defeat of Australia almost two weeks ago.

But the New Zealand coach agreed to give Fitzpatrick every chance to prove his fitness for what he termed one of the year's most important matches, to be played in front of an expected crowd of about 100,000 at the Melbourne Cricket Ground.
"Sean is desperate to play in this game," Hart said. "Bledisloe Cup matches are the high-point on the rugby calendar and this one is bigger than most."
If Fitzpatrick is ruled out, Norm Hewitt will start as hooker and number eight Zinzan Brooke will become captain.
New Zealand have not lost to the Wallabies since 1994.
